definitions.gloss: substitute; stand-in; someone who takes another's place
definitions.explanation: A person who takes the place of another, especially to bear punishment, danger, or hardship on their behalf. Can also refer to an object used as a protective substitute.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{身代|みが}わりになった。
{身代|みが}わり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人形|にんぎょう}→人形：01487_ningyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{置|お}いて→置く：01092_oku⟧⟦{逃|に}げた→逃げる：01151_nigeru⟧。
examples.english: He left a substitute doll and escaped.

examples.japanese: ⟦{王子|おうじ}→王子：01904_ouji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{身代|みが}わり⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{処刑|しょけい}→処刑：11757_shokei⟧⟦され→する：00392_suru⟧そうになった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{真実|しんじつ}→真実：05316_shinjitsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{明|あき}らか→明らか：02351_akiraka⟧になった。
examples.english: He was about to be executed as a stand-in for the prince, but the truth came to light at the last moment.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧ (body, self) + ⟦{代|か}わり→代わり：01296_kawari⟧ (substitute). Carries a dramatic nuance of self-sacrifice or deception.

In traditional Japanese culture, {身代|みが}わり{地蔵|じぞう} (substitute Jizo statues) are believed to take on illness or misfortune in place of a person. {身代|みが}わり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{守|まも}り→お守り：05955_omamori⟧ (protective charms) serve a similar function.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身代|みが}わり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become a substitute)
- {身代|みが}わり⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧ (to put up a stand-in)
- {身代|みが}わり{地蔵|じぞう} (substitute Jizo statue)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{代|か}わり→代わり：01296_kawari⟧: substitute, replacement (neutral, everyday)
- ⟦{替|か}え{玉|だま}→替え玉：08309_kaedama⟧: body double, fake substitute (often implies deception)
- ⟦{犠牲|ぎせい}→犠牲：14743_gisei⟧: sacrifice (emphasizes the cost or loss)
